status.scientific: interpretation of published definitions with finite countermodels

classification: interpretation of published definitions with finite countermodels
statement: Distinct key identifiers or declared lineage labels do not entail factorization of a joint probability law. Threshold authorization and probabilistic independence are separate properties.
observable: Two key identifiers, any supplied provenance grouping and a declared response domain
countermodels: A fair bit copied by both sources gives P(00)=P(11)=1/2
Two independent fair bits give all four joint states probability 1/4
Both models admit the same key identifiers and declared provenance labels
consequence: Metadata alone does not identify which joint law generated reports. Different labels are provenance declarations; a handed independent joint law proves independence only for that declared finite model, not causal identification of observed sources.
implementation: Vectors reuse published marginalInformation and exact rational arithmetic; no new estimator or authority evaluator
consumer: a structured-data consumer threshold and provenance contracts

formalEvidence.entropyValues: existing marginalInformation API; numeric vectors, not a new Lean entropy proof
